items.stem: What is meant by “transition elements”?
items.answer: Elements that have incompletely filled d orbitals in the ground state or in any of their common oxidation states.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: elements that have incompletely filled d orbitals in the ground state or in any of their common oxidation states.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about position and electronic configuration of transition elements is correct?
items.answer: The d-block occupies the middle of the periodic table, between groups 2 and 13.
items.markingKey: (b) The d-block occupies the middle of the periodic table, between groups 2 and 13. The other statements are false. Zn has 3d¹⁰ in the atom and in Zn²⁺, so it is not a transition element. The last electron enters the (n − 1)d subshell. Sc has the configuration 3d¹ 4s², an incomplete d subshell, so it is a transition element.
options: Scandium is not a transition element.
The d-block occupies the middle of the periodic table, between groups 2 and 13.
In transition elements the last electron enters the outermost (ns) shell.
Zinc is a transition element because it has electrons in the 3d subshell.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a main-group (s- or p-block) element?
items.answer: Fe
items.markingKey: (c) Fe is an element of the 3d series, not a main-group (s- or p-block) element.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In transition elements the last electron enters the outermost (ns) shell.”
items.answer: The last electron enters the (n − 1)d subshell.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The last electron enters the (n − 1)d subshell.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about position and electronic configuration of transition elements is incorrect?
items.answer: Copper has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁹ 4s².
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “Copper has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁹ 4s².” Correct form: Copper is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ because a filled 3d subshell is more stable.
options: The d-block occupies the middle of the periodic table, between groups 2 and 13.
Silver (4d¹⁰ 5s¹) is a transition element because Ag²⁺ has an incomplete 4d subshell.
Zinc, cadmium and mercury are not regarded as transition elements.

items.stem:
Neha studies the configuration of the first transition series.
(i) Write the configuration of Cr and Cu. (1 mark)
(ii) Why are they exceptional? (1 mark)
(iii) Which element of the series is not a transition element, and why? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Cr: [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹; Cu: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. (ii) Half-filled and fully filled d subshells are extra stable (exchange energy, symmetry). (iii) Zinc: 3d¹⁰ both in the atom and in Zn²⁺, so no incomplete d subshell.
items.markingKey: (i) 1 (ii) 1 (iii) 1 element + 1 reason.

items.stem: Which of the following is a main-group (s- or p-block) element?
items.answer: Sn
items.markingKey: (b) Sn is a main-group (s- or p-block) element; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of atomic number in the 3d series?
items.answer: Sc < Ti < Cu
items.markingKey: (d) Sc < Ti < Cu. Z increases from 21 (Sc) to 30 (Zn) across the series.

items.stem: Silver has a completely filled d subshell (4d¹⁰) in its ground state. How can you say that it is a transition element?
items.answer: Silver shows the +2 oxidation state (e.g. AgF₂), in which Ag²⁺ has an incomplete 4d⁹ configuration; so it fits the definition.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: +2 state; 1 mark: incomplete 4d⁹ fits the definition.

items.stem: What is the ground-state electronic configuration of zinc (Z = 30)?
items.answer: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s²
items.markingKey: (c) Zinc: [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s².

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Zinc is a transition element because it has electrons in the 3d subshell.”
items.answer: Zn has 3d¹⁰ in the atom and in Zn²⁺, so it is not a transition element.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Zn has 3d¹⁰ in the atom and in Zn²⁺, so it is not a transition element.

items.stem: How many d electrons are present in Ti³⁺ (Z of Ti = 22)? Is it paramagnetic or diamagnetic?
items.answer: d¹; paramagnetic
items.markingKey: (a) Ti³⁺: [Ar] 3d¹ (4s electrons are lost first) (1); 1 unpaired ⇒ paramagnetic (1).

items.stem: Define the term “inner transition elements”.
items.answer: The f-block elements, in which the 4f or 5f orbitals are progressively filled.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the f-block elements, in which the 4f or 5f orbitals are progressively filled.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Copper is a transition element because Cu²⁺ has a 3d⁹ configuration.
Reason (R): Copper has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁹ 4s².
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Copper is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ because a filled 3d subshell is more stable.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “an interstitial compound”?
items.answer: A compound formed when small atoms such as H, C or N are trapped in the crystal lattice of a metal.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a compound formed when small atoms such as H, C or N are trapped in the crystal lattice of a metal.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about general properties of transition elements is correct?
items.answer: Transition metals have high enthalpies of atomisation due to many unpaired electrons taking part in metallic bonding.
items.markingKey: (b) Transition metals have high enthalpies of atomisation due to many unpaired electrons taking part in metallic bonding. The other statements are false. d⁰ (Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺) and d¹⁰ (Cu⁺, Zn²⁺) ions are colourless. Zinc has the lowest; it has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding. Fe³⁺ (3d⁵, half-filled) is more stable than Fe²⁺ (3d⁶).
options: All transition metal ions are coloured.
Transition metals have high enthalpies of atomisation due to many unpaired electrons taking part in metallic bonding.
Zinc has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in the 3d series.
Fe³⁺ is less stable than Fe²⁺ because it has fewer electrons.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a transition metal catalyst?
items.answer: TiC
items.markingKey: (c) TiC is an interstitial compound, not a transition metal catalyst.
options: finely divided Fe in the Haber process

items.stem: A property of transition elements is explained as follows: ligands split the d orbitals; partly filled d orbitals; d–d transitions absorb visible light. Which property is being described? Give a reason.
items.answer: Colour of their compounds
items.markingKey: 1 mark: colour of their compounds; 1 mark: the features ligands split the d orbitals; partly filled d orbitals; d–d transitions absorb visible light are characteristic of it.

items.stem: A divalent or trivalent 3d ion has a spin-only magnetic moment of 5.92 BM. How many unpaired electrons does it have? Name one ion that fits.
items.answer: 5 unpaired electrons; e.g. Mn²⁺

items.stem: A property of transition elements is explained as follows: small atoms like H, C, N are trapped in voids; compounds are non-stoichiometric. Which property is being described?
items.answer: formation of interstitial compounds
items.markingKey: (c) Formation of interstitial compounds: small atoms like H, C, N are trapped in voids; compounds are non-stoichiometric.

items.stem: The E°(M²⁺/M) value for copper is positive (+0.34 V). What is the reason for this?
items.answer: Copper has a high enthalpy of atomisation and high ionisation enthalpies, which are not balanced by the hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺; so the overall change is unfavourable and E° is positive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: high ΔaH + IE; 1 mark: not compensated by hydration enthalpy.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct order of spin-only magnetic moment: Cu²⁺, Sc³⁺, Mn²⁺. Give a reason.
items.answer: Sc³⁺ < Cu²⁺ < Mn²⁺
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order Sc³⁺ < Cu²⁺ < Mn²⁺; 1 mark for the reason: μ increases with the number of unpaired electrons: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

items.stem: Which term describes a blend of metals made by mixing the components, often of transition metals with similar atomic radii?
items.answer: an alloy
items.markingKey: (a) An alloy: a blend of metals made by mixing the components, often of transition metals with similar atomic radii.

items.stem: Which of the following is a coloured ion in aqueous solution?
items.answer: Cu²⁺
items.markingKey: (c) Cu²⁺ is a coloured ion in aqueous solution; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following is an interstitial compound?
items.answer: Fe₃H
items.markingKey: (a) Fe₃H is an interstitial compound; the others are not.
options: finely divided Fe in the Haber process

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Fe³⁺ is less stable than Fe²⁺ because it has fewer electrons.”
items.answer: Fe³⁺ (3d⁵, half-filled) is more stable than Fe²⁺ (3d⁶).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Fe³⁺ (3d⁵, half-filled) is more stable than Fe²⁺ (3d⁶).

items.stem: Explain giving reasons: (i) transition metals form a large number of complex compounds; (ii) the lowest oxide of a transition metal is basic and the highest is acidic; (iii) transition metals show variable oxidation states; (iv) Cr²⁺ is reducing while Mn³⁺ is oxidising, though both are d⁴; (v) Sc³⁺ is colourless.
items.answer: (i) Small, highly charged ions with vacant d orbitals of suitable energy. (ii) In higher oxidation states bonding becomes covalent, e.g. MnO basic, Mn₂O₇ acidic. (iii) (n − 1)d and ns electrons have similar energies, so different numbers can be lost. (iv) Cr²⁺ → Cr³⁺ gives stable d³ (half-filled t₂g); Mn³⁺ → Mn²⁺ gives stable d⁵. (v) 3d⁰: no d–d transition.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for (i)–(v).

items.stem: What is meant by “diamagnetism”?
items.answer: The weak repulsion of a substance by a magnetic field, shown when all electrons are paired.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the weak repulsion of a substance by a magnetic field, shown when all electrons are paired.

items.stem: Give two differences between formation of interstitial compounds and catalytic activity.
items.answer: Formation of interstitial compounds: compounds are non-stoichiometric; formed by elements such as Ti and Mn (TiC, Mn₄N). Catalytic activity: formation of unstable intermediates; large surface area for adsorption.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. formation of interstitial compounds – compounds are non-stoichiometric; formed by elements such as Ti and Mn (TiC, Mn₄N); catalytic activity – formation of unstable intermediates; large surface area for adsorption.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a coloured ion in aqueous solution?
items.answer: Sc³⁺
items.markingKey: (a) Sc³⁺ is a colourless ion in aqueous solution, not a coloured ion in aqueous solution.

items.stem: A property of transition elements is explained as follows: very hard with high melting points; compounds are non-stoichiometric. Which property is being described? Give a reason.
items.answer: Formation of interstitial compounds
items.markingKey: 1 mark: formation of interstitial compounds; 1 mark: the features very hard with high melting points; compounds are non-stoichiometric are characteristic of it.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Zinc has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in the 3d series.”
items.answer: Zinc has the lowest; it has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Zinc has the lowest; it has no unpaired d electrons for metallic bonding.

items.stem: Define the term “the chromate–dichromate equilibrium”.
items.answer: The pH-dependent interconversion 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the pH-dependent interconversion 2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate is correct?
items.answer: Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ turns green when it oxidises SO₂ or H₂S.
items.markingKey: (c) Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ turns green when it oxidises SO₂ or H₂S. The other statements are false. KMnO₄ is not a primary standard (it decomposes slowly); K₂Cr₂O₇ is used as a primary standard. It is reduced to Cr³⁺, gaining 6 electrons per ion. MnO₄⁻ (Mn⁺⁷, d⁰) is diamagnetic; its colour is due to charge transfer.
options: In acidic medium Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to Cr²⁺.
KMnO₄ is used as a primary standard in volumetric analysis.
Acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ turns green when it oxidises SO₂ or H₂S.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Adding alkali to a dichromate solution turns it orange.
Reason (R): In acidic medium MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons to form Mn²⁺.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Alkali converts dichromate to yellow chromate. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: An oxidising agent has these properties: dark purple crystals; acts as a self-indicator in titrations; in acid gains 5 electrons to give Mn²⁺. Identify the compound. Give a reason.
items.answer: Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)
items.markingKey: 1 mark: potassium permanganate (KMnO₄); 1 mark: the features dark purple crystals; acts as a self-indicator in titrations; in acid gains 5 electrons to give Mn²⁺ are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Titrations of KMnO₄ are not carried out in the presence of HCl.
Reason (R): HCl is oxidised to chlorine by permanganate.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Part of KMnO₄ would be consumed by HCl, giving wrong results.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
An oxidising agent has these properties: green compound; Mn in the +6 state; disproportionates in acid to MnO₄⁻ and MnO₂.
(i) Identify the compound. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇)? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄) (ii) paramagnetic with one unpaired electron (iii) orange crystals; made from chromite ore via Na₂CrO₄
items.markingKey: (i) potassium manganate (K₂MnO₄) – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: paramagnetic with one unpaired electron – 1 mark. (iii) for potassium dichromate (K₂Cr₂O₇): orange crystals; made from chromite ore via Na₂CrO₄; in acid gains 6 electrons to give green Cr³⁺ – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Describe the preparation of potassium dichromate from chromite ore. What is the effect of increasing pH on a solution of potassium dichromate? Write the reaction of acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ with Fe²⁺.
items.answer: 4FeCr₂O₄ + 8Na₂CO₃ + 7O₂ → 8Na₂CrO₄ + 2Fe₂O₃ + 8CO₂; 2Na₂CrO₄ + 2H⁺ → Na₂Cr₂O₇ + 2Na⁺ + H₂O; Na₂Cr₂O₇ + 2KCl → K₂Cr₂O₇ + 2NaCl. Increasing pH converts orange dichromate to yellow chromate. Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O.
items.markingKey: 3 marks preparation; 1 mark pH effect; 1 mark Fe²⁺ equation.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The permanganate ion is paramagnetic.”
items.answer: MnO₄⁻ (Mn⁺⁷, d⁰) is diamagnetic; its colour is due to charge transfer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: MnO₄⁻ (Mn⁺⁷, d⁰) is diamagnetic; its colour is due to charge transfer.

items.stem: Explain the term “a self-indicator”.
items.answer: A titrant whose own colour change marks the end point, as KMnO₄ does.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a titrant whose own colour change marks the end point, as KMnO₄ does.

items.stem: An oxidising agent has these properties: dark purple crystals; made from pyrolusite via green K₂MnO₄. Identify the compound.
items.answer: potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)
items.markingKey: (b) Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄): dark purple crystals; made from pyrolusite via green K₂MnO₄.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence in the manufacture of K₂Cr₂O₇: Na₂Cr₂O₇, K₂Cr₂O₇, Na₂CrO₄, FeCr₂O₄ (chromite). Give a reason.
items.answer: FeCr₂O₄ (chromite) → Na₂CrO₄ → Na₂Cr₂O₇ → K₂Cr₂O₇
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order FeCr₂O₄ (chromite) → Na₂CrO₄ → Na₂Cr₂O₇ → K₂Cr₂O₇; 1 mark for the reason: Fusion with Na₂CO₃ in air, acidification with H₂SO₄, then double decomposition with KCl.

items.stem: Aisha titrates 10 mL of a 0.05 M solution of iodide (as KI) with 0.02 M acidified K₂Cr₂O₇. Using the equation Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6I⁻ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3I₂ + 7H₂O, calculate the volume of oxidant needed.
items.markingKey: mol of reductant = 10 × 0.05/1000 = 5.00 × 10⁻⁴ mol (1); mol Cr₂O₇²⁻ = 1/6 × that = 8.33 × 10⁻⁵ mol (1); V = n/M = 4.17 mL (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is a compound of manganese in the +7 state?
items.answer: NaMnO₄
items.markingKey: (d) NaMnO₄ is a compound of manganese in the +7 state; the others are not.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) and potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄) on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An oxidising agent has these properties: stable in alkaline medium. Identify the compound – potassium permanganate (KMnO₄) or potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄)? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄): dark purple crystals; made from pyrolusite via green K₂MnO₄; in acid gains 5 electrons to give Mn²⁺. Potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄): yellow compound; stable in alkaline medium; turns orange on acidification. (b) Potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄); 1 mark: “stable in alkaline medium” is a feature of potassium chromate (K₂CrO₄).

items.stem: What is meant by “lanthanoid contraction”?
items.answer: The steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium, due to poor shielding by 4f electrons.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium, due to poor shielding by 4f electrons.

items.stem: What is the electronic configuration of thulium (Z = 69)?
items.answer: [Xe] 4f¹³ 6s²
items.markingKey: (a) Thulium: [Xe] 4f¹³ 6s². La, Ce, Gd and Lu keep one 5d electron; the others are [Xe] 4fⁿ 6s².

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Ionic radii of Ln³⁺ ions increase from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺.
Reason (R): Actinoids show a greater range of oxidation states than lanthanoids.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: They decrease steadily from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺ (lanthanoid contraction). R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A series of elements shows these features: oxidation states vary widely, up to +7 for Mn; 3d orbitals are filled; includes iron, cobalt and nickel. Which series is described? Give a reason.
items.answer: The 3d transition series
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the 3d transition series; 1 mark: the features oxidation states vary widely, up to +7 for Mn; 3d orbitals are filled; includes iron, cobalt and nickel are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Give two differences between the lanthanoids and the actinoids.
items.answer: The lanthanoids: mostly non-radioactive (except promethium); oxidation states +2 and +4 only where f⁰, f⁷ or f¹⁴ results. The actinoids: 5f orbitals are filled; all are radioactive.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the lanthanoids – mostly non-radioactive (except promethium); oxidation states +2 and +4 only where f⁰, f⁷ or f¹⁴ results; the actinoids – 5f orbitals are filled; all are radioactive.

items.stem:
Aditi compares the chemistry of the lanthanoids and actinoids for a project.
(i) Which series shows the wider range of oxidation states? (1 mark)
(ii) Give one reason for your answer. (1 mark)
(iii) Why is the separation of lanthanoids difficult, and give one use of a lanthanoid alloy. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Actinoids. (ii) 5f, 6d and 7s orbitals are comparable in energy. (iii) Lanthanoid contraction gives very similar sizes and chemistry; misch metal is used in lighter flints and Mg-based alloys for bullets and shells.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Lanthanoid contraction is caused by increased shielding by 4f electrons.”
items.answer: It is caused by imperfect (poor) shielding by 4f electrons as nuclear charge increases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It is caused by imperfect (poor) shielding by 4f electrons as nuclear charge increases.

items.stem: Compare the lanthanoids and actinoids with respect to (i) electronic configuration, (ii) oxidation states, (iii) atomic and ionic sizes, (iv) radioactivity and (v) chemical reactivity.
items.answer: (i) Ln: [Xe] 4f¹⁻¹⁴ 5d⁰⁻¹ 6s²; An: [Rn] 5f¹⁻¹⁴ 6d⁰⁻¹ 7s². (ii) Ln mainly +3; An +3 to +7. (iii) Both contract; actinoid contraction is larger. (iv) Ln non-radioactive except Pm; all An are radioactive. (v) Actinoids are more reactive, especially when finely divided.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for (i)–(v).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an actinoid?
items.answer: hafnium
items.markingKey: (d) Hafnium is a d-block element, not an actinoid.

items.stem: Write the electronic configuration of Lu³⁺ (lutetium, Z = 71) and state the number of unpaired electrons.
items.answer: [Xe] 4f¹⁴; 0 unpaired
items.markingKey: Ln³⁺ ions have the configuration [Xe] 4f¹⁴ (Z − 57 = 14 f electrons) (1); unpaired electrons = 0 (1).

items.stem: Which of the following is an actinoid?
items.answer: neptunium
items.markingKey: (d) Neptunium is an actinoid; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about lanthanoids and actinoids is correct?
items.answer: All actinoids are radioactive.
items.markingKey: (c) All actinoids are radioactive. The other statements are false. Actinoids show more oxidation states because 5f, 6d and 7s levels are close in energy. 5f orbitals extend further (are less buried) than 4f orbitals. They decrease steadily from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺ (lanthanoid contraction).
options: Lanthanoids show more oxidation states than actinoids.
Ionic radii of Ln³⁺ ions increase from La³⁺ to Lu³⁺.
The 4f orbitals penetrate further into the core than 5f orbitals.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Zr and Hf have very similar properties.
Reason (R): Lanthanoid contraction makes their atomic radii nearly equal.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Similar size ⇒ similar chemistry.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Explain the term “lanthanoid contraction”.
items.answer: The steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium, due to poor shielding by 4f electrons.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the steady decrease in atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium, due to poor shielding by 4f electrons.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct order of spin-only magnetic moment?
items.answer: Sc³⁺ < Cu²⁺ < Fe²⁺
items.markingKey: (b) Sc³⁺ < Cu²⁺ < Fe²⁺. μ increases with the number of unpaired electrons: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

items.stem: What is the oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄?
items.markingKey: (d) Sum of oxidation numbers = 0 ⇒ Mn = +7 in KMnO₄.

items.stem: Which term describes an alloy of about 95% lanthanoid metal with iron and traces of S, C, Ca and Al, used in lighter flints?
items.answer: misch metal
items.markingKey: (a) Misch metal: an alloy of about 95% lanthanoid metal with iron and traces of S, C, Ca and Al, used in lighter flints.

(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)

items.stem: A series of elements shows these features: includes iron, cobalt and nickel; oxidation states vary widely, up to +7 for Mn; many ions are coloured due to d–d transitions. Which series is described? Give a reason.
items.answer: The 3d transition series
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the 3d transition series; 1 mark: the features includes iron, cobalt and nickel; oxidation states vary widely, up to +7 for Mn; many ions are coloured due to d–d transitions are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following ions is coloured in aqueous solution?
items.answer: Fe²⁺
items.markingKey: (a) Fe²⁺ is d⁶ with partly filled d orbitals, so d–d transitions absorb visible light.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Scandium is a transition element.
Reason (R): Sc³⁺ has an incompletely filled 3d subshell.
